reason: E1 and E2 support the entropy-stabilization premise, and E3 provides direct evidence for thermal stability of HEA nanoparticles up to 1000 K, but no cited evidence addresses the role of lattice distortion, the existence of a distortion threshold, or the specific synthesis method, leaving key mechanistic premises unsupported.
premises: High configurational entropy stabilizes disordered solid-solution phases in HEAs, especially at high temperatures.
Lattice distortion from atomic size mismatches can drive short-range ordering or phase segregation.
A threshold exists for lattice distortion beyond which enthalpic forces overcome entropic stabilization.
HEA nanoparticles can be synthesized as homogeneous solid solutions via rapid thermal processing.
Structural stability of HEA nanoparticles can be maintained from 573 to 1000 K.
